_meta.note: Continuation of the code adapter (Seam 1 = dep-lint, done: GATE_C0/GATE_C1). Two deliverables: (c) SEAM 2 — feed code context to Stage B; and (a) the ADAPTER ARCHITECTURE doc. Seam 2 is built as a GENERIC, domain-neutral context hook in BOTH executors (py executor.py assemble_context + node hb-exec.js assembleContext): when a `context_cmd` is configured (HB_EXEC_CONTEXT_CMD / executor.json context_cmd) the executor runs it per task and appends its stdout to the task's context before dispatch. The executor stays code-AGNOSTIC (a boundary gate forbids it mentioning codegraph/deplint). `codegraph-context.js` is the FIRST provider — node-only, adapter-owned, gated hermetically. PARITY: the context-injection mechanism is a NEW shared behavioral surface, so it is mirrored in both runtimes and asserted node==python by a parity proof (recorded in parity-notes). OLLAMA (llama3.2:3b et al. available locally) drives a real end-to-end demo, but harness-first / on-demand only — it needs a model and is non-deterministic, so it is NOT in the gated suite; the injection MECHANISM is gated deterministically with stubs. The code provider itself stays node-only / not a parity surface (like Seam 1). Spec-first; adversarial review on both gates.

phases.title: Seam 2 — code context to Stage B (generic hook, both runtimes)

tasks.title: Author the Seam-2 proofs + fixtures + stubs (spec-first)
tasks.description: Spec-first, two proofs that MUST fail before the code lands. (A) docs/howto/gate-examples/code-context.sh — add a DEDICATED fixture plugin/adapters/code/fixtures/context.codemap.json with >=4 symbols and a clear UNRELATED one, e.g. edges [["symA","symB"],["symZ","symA"],["symU","symB"]], tasks {"TA":["symA"]} — so for task TA (symA) the DIRECT neighbors are symB (A depends on) and symZ (uses A), while symU is NOT a direct neighbor of symA (it only touches symB). `node plugin/adapters/code/codegraph-context.js <context.codemap.json> TA` must emit a readable block that names symA AND its direct neighbors symB and symZ, and MUST NOT name symU — proving a real SUBGRAPH (direct neighbors), not an echo of the task's own symbols and not the whole graph. Assert symB present, symZ present, symU ABSENT. Marker CODE-CONTEXT-OK; fails before codegraph-context.js exists. (B) docs/howto/gate-examples/context-inject-parity.sh — proves the GENERIC hook injects a configured command's output into the task payload IDENTICALLY on both runtimes. The context_cmd stub is deliberately a GENERIC, NON-CODE command that prints delimited output `<<HBCTX>>CODECTX:<taskid><<HBCTX>>` (reading the id from the env the executor sets) — its non-code-ness is what proves the hook is generic (not codegraph-specific). A backend stub (execute mode: read payload JSON on stdin, write payload.context to a file, print {"ok":true,"summary":"done"}). Bootstrap ONE throwaway project (HB_NO_GIT=1, shared by both legs) with ONE ready task; configure context_cmd + the stub backend; run the NODE executor (node .hb/hb-exec.js run, HB_EXEC_MAX_ITERS=1) and the PYTHON executor (python -m heartbeat.cli exec run --dir, HB_EXEC_MAX_ITERS=1) each once, capturing the payload context each time. Extract the DELIMITED injected block (between the <<HBCTX>> markers) from each capture and assert: (i) it contains CODECTX:<taskid> on BOTH, and (ii) the node injected block EQUALS the python injected block. Compare ONLY the delimited injected block, NOT the whole assembled context (node's assembleContext appends a git-log block python does not — a pre-existing node-only divergence; comparing whole contexts would be environment-fragile). set -euo pipefail + explicit exits; skip cleanly if node/python3 absent; marker CONTEXT-INJECT-PARITY-OK; fails before the executor hook exists. Fast (<5s): one shared bootstrap, stubs, MAX_ITERS=1.

tasks.title: Implement the codegraph-context provider
tasks.description: Create plugin/adapters/code/codegraph-context.js: pure module contextFor(codemap, taskId) -> a readable context string. It takes the codemap ({edges:[[from,to]], tasks:{TASKID:[sym...]}}), finds the symbols the task touches, and renders a subgraph: for each touched symbol, its direct dependencies (edges from it) and dependents (edges to it), as human-readable lines an agent can use (e.g. 'symA depends on: symB' / 'symA is used by: symZ'). CLI: `node codegraph-context.js <codemap.json> <TASKID>` prints the block. Pure Node stdlib only; imports nothing from core (boundary, gated by GATE_S2). This is the first PROVIDER for the generic executor context hook.

tasks.title: Add the generic context hook to the Python executor
tasks.description: Extend py/src/heartbeat/executor.py with a GENERIC, domain-neutral context hook (NO mention of codegraph/deplint — the executor just runs a configured command). config(hbdir) gains `context_cmd` (env HB_EXEC_CONTEXT_CMD > executor.json context_cmd > empty). assemble_context(hbdir, task): when context_cmd is set, run it (subprocess; pass the task id/title/description via env like HB_TASK_ID/HB_TASK_TITLE/HB_TASK_DESC), capture stdout, and APPEND it to the assembled context wrapped in a STABLE delimiter (the same markers node uses, so the injected block is extractable and byte-comparable across runtimes). Degrade cleanly if the command errors (log to stderr, don't crash the task). Keep the existing context behavior unchanged when context_cmd is empty. Add/extend a python test in py/tests/test_exec.py asserting a configured context_cmd's stdout appears in the dispatched payload's context.

tasks.title: Add the same generic context hook to the node executor
tasks.description: Extend plugin/templates/hb-exec.js with the SAME generic hook so behavior matches Python (parity). config() gains contextCmd (HB_EXEC_CONTEXT_CMD > executor.json context_cmd > empty). assembleContext(task): when contextCmd is set, run it (child process; pass HB_TASK_ID/HB_TASK_TITLE/HB_TASK_DESC in env), capture stdout, append it to the context wrapped in the SAME stable delimiter markers as Python (so the injected block is byte-identical across runtimes) and with the same semantics. Domain-neutral (no codegraph/deplint mention). Degrade cleanly on error. Unchanged when contextCmd is empty.

tasks.title: Wire the deterministic proofs (T88/T89), add the on-demand ollama demo, record parity
tasks.description: Add node-suite group T88 (code-context.sh -> CODE-CONTEXT-OK) and T89 (context-inject-parity.sh -> CONTEXT-INJECT-PARITY-OK) to tests/run-tests.sh (guard on node, and T89 on python3). Add an ON-DEMAND, harness-first demo tests/real-context.sh: with a real ollama backend (HB_EXEC_BACKEND ollama-ish, HB_EXEC_MODEL=llama3.2:3b, OLLAMA available) and context_cmd wired to codegraph-context.js over a fixture codemap, dispatch one task and show the model's run carried the code context (grep the dispatched payload/context) — clearly documented as NOT gated (needs ollama, non-deterministic), skips cleanly if ollama is absent. Record in planning/parity-notes.md that the executor CONTEXT-INJECTION hook is a shared BEHAVIORAL surface mirrored in both runtimes (parity proof T89), while the codegraph-context provider is node-only / not a parity surface (like the rest of the code adapter). Keep node suite, python suite (test_exec.py), and tests/parity.sh all green.

tasks.title: Write the adapter architecture concept doc
tasks.description: Write docs/adapters.md — a first-class concept doc presenting the ADAPTER ARCHITECTURE: the HeartBeat method (DAG+gates+tick) is domain-agnostic; domain intelligence enters through ADAPTERS at two defined SEAMS — (1) plan authoring (validate the task DAG against the domain's real dependency graph; the codemap contract; deplint) and (2) context assembly (feed the domain's knowledge to Stage B via the generic context_cmd hook). Explain the codemap contract ({edges, tasks}) is domain-neutral (ids are opaque units, not necessarily code), so the SAME engine generalizes; give non-code examples (data lineage, IaC, research citations). State the BOUNDARY rules (adapters live in plugin/adapters/, not scaffolded, not core, not a parity surface, import nothing from core, suites green without them). Name CODE as the first domain and reference its proofs (code-deplint.sh, code-map.sh, code-context.sh) and the parity proof for the shared hook. Be HONEST and explicit: the live CodeGraph DB read and the ollama Seam-2 demo are harness-first / on-demand — NOT gated or proven in-repo; what IS gated is the pure mapping, the dep-lint engine, the context provider, and the node==python injection mechanism. Present non-code adapters (data lineage, IaC, research) as the PATTERN generalizing, NOT as shipped providers (only the code adapter exists). Add a pointer to docs/adapters.md from README.md. Must pass prose-check (links resolve, only real hb subcommands, substantive). (Honesty is verified by the GATE_AD adversarial review, not by a criterion — state claims you can defend.)
